prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t say one single company is definitively “the best” for every situation, but I can help you find the best match. The right choice depends on your ZIP code, the exact problem, budget, warranty status, and whether you need emergency service. If you tell me your neighborhood or ZIP I can give 3–5 well-reviewed local options and recent typical pricing.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide to help you pick a top HVAC company in Houston:

What to look for
- Proper licensing and insurance (TX license/registration and liability insurance).  
- NATE- or EPA-certified technicians.  
- Good recent reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi, and BBB (watch for responses to complaints).  
- Clear, written estimates and warranties on parts and labor.  
- Availability for emergency/after-hours service if you need it fast.  
- Transparent pricing (diagnostic fee, hourly rates, flat-fee options).  
- Experience with your system brand and refrigerant type (R-22 vs R-410A).

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed/insured? Can you provide license number?  
- What is your diagnostic fee and is it waived if I hire you?  
- Do you guarantee your work (parts/labor warranty length)?  
- How long to arrive (same day/emergency)?  
- Are technicians background-checked/insured?  
- Will I get a written estimate before work begins?  
- Do you offer financing or maintenance plans?

Typical repair price ranges (Houston—approximate)
- Diagnostic/Service call: $75–$200  
- Capacitor/contactors/fuses: $100–$350  
- Refrigerant recharge (R-410A): $150–$400 (depends on amount)  
- Evaporator/condenser coil or major mechanical repairs: $800–$2,500+  
- Compressor replacement or major outdoor unit repair: $1,000–$3,000+  
(If repair costs approach 50% or more of a new system, replacement is often more economical long-term.)

Red flags
- Technician refuses to provide written estimate or ID.  
- Company demands full cash up front.  
- Very low quote compared to competitors without explanation.  
- Lots of unresolved negative reviews or complaints to the BBB.

If you want, tell me:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood  
- Symptoms (not cooling, short-cycling, leaks, noises, high bills)  
- Age of the AC and any warranty/maintenance history

I’ll then suggest a short list of top local companies and what to expect from each.
